purpose: One-shot 550-nm MYSTIC diagnostic of aerosol vertical-shape sensitivity for the Taylor late-twilight rows. Hold each row's independently frozen AOD550 and all other modeled quantities fixed; replace only the aerosol optical-depth vertical distribution with the independently retrieved NOAA HRRR-Smoke vertical shape.

hrrr.profileConstruction: Join HRRR nat-file HGT and MASSDEN by hybrid level for 01:00 and 02:00 UTC; define AGL height relative to hybrid-level-1 HGT; retain exactly 50 levels; interpolate density in AGL height and linearly in UTC to each Taylor row; integrate rho dz within the common 0.262,1,2,...,120 km libRadtran atmosphere layers; normalize above-observer layer masses to sum exactly 1.0 and use them only as the relative optical-depth vertical distribution before applying the already-frozen row AOD550.
hrrr.columnSanity: For each bracketing HRRR analysis, the 50-level trapezoidal rho dz column must agree with HRRR COLMD within 2 percent before any MYSTIC call.
hrrr.interpretation: HRRR smoke mass is a vertical-shape proxy only. This does not assert that all aerosol was smoke, that smoke mass is a calibrated extinction coefficient, or that HRRR is the exact CAMS total-aerosol profile.

AFGLUS molecular atmosphere and 0.262-km observer treatment
comparison.primaryDiagnostic: deltaMag550 = -2.5*log10(Q_hrrr_shape/Q_default_vertical); positive means the lower HRRR-shaped aerosol makes the modeled twilight darker at 550 nm.
comparison.broadbandOrientationOnly: For scale/direction only, deltaMag550 is added to the already frozen broadband SQM model magnitude. This is explicitly not a new broadband SQM forward calculation or validation.

stopping: Run exactly the frozen 10 rows once at GitHub run attempt 1. No GitHub re-run, no same-identity retry, no AOD/profile tuning, no result-dependent row change, and no result-dependent change of photon budget.
